description: S59 T6 (EV17) at the DOOR, before any service runs: params carrying `actor` are refused with the transport's bad-params code and the refusal NAMES the key. The actor is the connection's peer, taken from the socket's peer credentials (P26); a caller that could name an author could write the audit as somebody who was not there. fromDoor is why the walker dispatches this one against a HEALTHY seam — the refusal must happen whether or not a service exists. The refusal is a transport-level condition, so it keeps JSON-RPC's own code and carries no `data` (conformance/README): the shape of params is a protocol fact, not an Aeon refusal with a kind a client branches on.

error.message: invalid params: environment.create params carry "actor" — the caller names what to act on, never who acted, when it happened, which origin it carries, or where a value lives (S59 EV7, EV17)
